title: Chargers camp day 1: Justin Herbert comfortable in offense, O'Leary's defense flying, & Tuipulotu sits out
description: The Sporting Tribune's Fernando Ramirez writes about the comfortability of quarterback Justin Herbert in McDaniel's scheme and more from day one of camp.
fullText:
El SEGUNDO, Calif. -- It wouldn’t be the first day of training camp without Jim Harbaugh using some sort of metaphor. On Wednesday, he compared the first day of camp to a "family reunion" and "Christmas morning."

Harbaugh is entering his third year building the Chargers alongside general manager Joe Hortiz. Only 14 of the 90 players on the roster remain from the Tom Telesco era.

"We all feel the same thing," Harbaugh said. "It's that feeling like, 'We're capable. We are more than capable.’”

This training camp feels different from previous years, and much of that has to do with the excitement surrounding new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel.

McDaniel walked onto the practice field about 20 minutes before the 10 a.m. PT start. He made his way around to every position group, greeting players with handshakes and daps while spending several minutes talking with them. He was all smiles throughout.

Even quarterback Justin Herbert appears energized by McDaniel and the new offense. While he appreciated the month away from football, he admitted he was eager to get back.

"I thought having a month off was great to be able to go through the iPad and go through exactly everything that we need to," Herbert said. "Guys have picked it up really quickly… So that allows us to be fast out there and go play football."

During OTAs, McDaniel said he wanted Herbert to adjust his footwork by lining up with his left foot forward and his right foot back in the shotgun.

Jessica Cryderman - The Sporting Tribune

Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) talking with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniels during Chargers training camp at the Bolt on Wednesday, July 29th in El Segundo, CA.

Herbert continued working on those mechanics while back home in Eugene, Oregon, where he threw with his brother, Patrick, who is attending the Jacksonville Jaguars' training camp as a tight end.

"You get to the point where you're not thinking about it," Herbert said. "You go out to practice and you're just throwing the ball and now you can worry about mechanics, how am I throwing the ball, where is it going, routes and things like that. As opposed to months ago, it was making sure your feet are lined up with the routes, timing. There was a lot that went into it but now you're just playing football."

The changes to the offense were noticeable from the start of practice, but they became especially apparent during 11-on-11 drills. After Herbert called the play, the offense quickly sprinted to the line of scrimmage and snapped the ball.

On the first 11-on-11 play, Herbert faked a pitch before finding rookie wide receiver Brenen Thompson for a short gain.

Earlier during 7-on-7 drills, Herbert narrowly missed Thompson on a deep ball. The two connected several more times throughout practice, including one sideline throw that Thompson secured with a sliding catch before going out of bounds.

"He's going to be very good," Herbert said. "We saw it early on that he was skilled, he's fast, he's going to make a lot of plays for us. I'm really excited about him."

So far, Herbert and McDaniel appear to be off to a strong start.

The Chargers defense enters the season with several question marks following the departure of defensive coordinator Jesse Minter. The team promoted 34-year-old Chris O'Leary to lead the defense, and players have expressed excitement about working with him again after his previous stint with the Chargers in 2024.

Several defenders have praised O'Leary's aggressive style and believe the unit can remain one of the team's strengths.

"He's not holding back, he's not shy," Chargers safety Derwin James said. "I feel like a lot of people are going to get to see who he really is this year. I'm confident in him."

Jessica Cryderman - The Sporting Tribune

Los Angeles Chargers safety Derwin James Jr. (3) during Chargers training camp at the Bolt on Wednesday, July 29th in El Segundo, CA.

During 11-on-11 drills, backup quarterback Trey Lance attempted a deep pass over the middle, but cornerback Tarheeb Still came away with an interception, the second takeaway of training camp. The first interception belonged to cornerback Isas Waxter, who also picked off Lance.

Still and fellow third-year cornerback Cam Hart are two players James believes are poised to take another step in their development.

"Year 3 is usually when you have to take that next step," James said. "I've been telling him that Year 3 is a pivotal year, not that any year isn't pivotal, but I feel like this is how you shape your career on who you're going to be."

Tuipulotu working off to the side

The only player who did not participate in the first day of training camp was outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu.

Tuipulotu worked off to the side while the rest of the team practiced.

It appears to be a hold-in situation as the former second-round pick enters his fourth season after recording a career-high 13 sacks in 2025.

"It's just the process of it, man," James said. "The team loves him. We love Tuli. I knew the team loved me too when I had the same similar situation, but sometimes that stuff takes longer to iron out."

James did the same thing in 2022 before he got his pay day.

Hortiz is familiar with these situations. Last year, left tackle Rashawn Slater held in before signing an extension that made him the highest-paid offensive tackle in the NFL.

Beyond the start of training camp, there was another reason for excitement surrounding Herbert, who recently proposed to his girlfriend, singer Madison Beer.

"We didn't know until after, we were all in the quarterback room and he told us," Harbaugh said. "He had kind of said it was going to happen this summer and everything.”

Herbert and the pop star have been together since 2025. The day before training camp opened, Beer shared proposal photos with the Chargers quarterback early in the morning.

"Man, I was happy for him,” James said. “I was tweeting at like 7 a.m. when I saw it. He told me he was going to do it… So it was fun to see."

Jessica Cryderman - The Sporting Tribune

Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert addresses media during Chargers training camp at the Bolt on Wednesday, July 29th in El Segundo, CA.

Herbert made his first NFL start in Week 2 of his rookie season after then-starting quarterback Tyrod Taylor suffered a medical emergency.

When asked Wednesday whether he was more nervous before proposing or before getting just 90 seconds' notice to make his NFL debut, Herbert didn't hesitate.

"The proposal, for sure," Herbert said with a smile.

title: Biggest question for the Cowboys after start of training camp
description: What questions did Day 1 of camp bring in your opinion?
fullText:
The long wait is finally over. The Dallas Cowboys have not only reported to Oxnard, California for training camp, but have now officially kicked things off with their first practice Wednesday afternoon. And for all of us starving for some clarity on some unanswered questions about this year’s team, Day 1 of training camp didn’t disappoint.

Among some of the things we learned from Day 1 in training camp is Caleb Downs will play an important, versatile role as a rookie, the RB2 competition is heating up, how the secondary might line up, and Tyler Booker looks primed for a big year. The biggest remaining unanswered question though revolves around Quinnen Williams.

The Dallas Cowboys paid a hefty price to acquire Quinnen Williams from the New York Jets a season ago and he’s expected to be the foundational centerpiece Dallas’ defense continues to build around. He was just named to the leadership council in this year, and as we recently learned is at the top of the Cowboys list for a contract extension.

Stephen Jones made it very clear in Tuesday’s press conference they are not only open, but want, Quinnen Williams for the long haul. In fact, they’ve apparently already reached out to his agent.

Cowboys EVP Stephen Jones said DT Quinnen Williams is at the top of the list of players they want to get signed long term.

“Absolutely. We’re very open to that. We want Quinnen here for the long haul.” 

They’ve already had talks with his agent.

— Jon Machota (@jonmachota) July 28, 2026

Even though Williams claims he’s more focused on training camp, his first with the Cowboys, and building the defense than he is in extension talk, there seems to be mutual interest between both parties. Addressing the media after practice Wednesday, he even confirmed he wanted to be with the Cowboys “for the long haul”.

Cowboys DT Quinnen Williams said Dallas is “for sure” where he wants to be long term. “I definitely want to be here for the long haul. I want to win.” pic.twitter.com/4UnJE0pj4D

— Jon Machota (@jonmachota) July 29, 2026

Of the players next in line to earn a potential long-term extension from the Cowboys, Williams should be at the top of the list. He is not only one of the best interior defensive lineman in the entire league, but someone they can continue to build around for years to come. But, what makes this so interesting is the bombshell Jerry Jones dropped yesterday hinting a “substantive” trade could possibly be in the works in the not-too-distant future.

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he talked with an owner of another team yesterday about a “substantive” deal. He says he sees value in bargaining future assets to improve this team. pic.twitter.com/9HO0vZTw1C

— Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) July 28, 2026

If the Cowboys are once again circling back to Maxx Crosby to potentially acquire him via trade like many believe, the Cowboys would have to do some serious salary-cap finagling to extend Williams and absorb Crosby’s contract as well. That’s not even mentioning anyone else they could be considering locking up long-term at the end of the 2026 season.

As training camp continues to progress and we continue to learn more and more about the Dallas Cowboys, the Quinnen Williams’ long-term contract situation will remain a big unanswered question. Thankfully, there’s no need to worry about his on the field production or how he’ll fit in Christian Parker’s new 3-4 defense. His contract situation though is interesting.

title: Skubal Hits 1,000 Ks But The Real Reason Fans Are Devastated
description: Tarik Skubal struck out his 1,000th batter to earn a roar, but the Tigers face a trade deadline that could send him away.
fullText:
Tarik Skubal hit a massive milestone Wednesday night, but don’t let the applause fool you—this feels bittersweet for Detroit fans. In the first inning against the Orioles, Taylor Ward swung and missed to log the pitcher’s 1,000th career whiff. The crowd exploded immediately, giving the ace a standing ovation that shook Comerica Park. It’s a career high point, yet it might be his final act in a Tigers uniform.

The jumbotron flashed a tribute image alongside his signature while the arena buzzed with energy. “1,000 career strikeouts. Tarik Skubal” scrolled across the screen for everyone to see. That’s a perfect send-off for a guy who’s dominated the league, even if the front office won’t keep him much longer. The Tigers’ 22-40 start earlier this year made it nearly certain Skubal would be traded before the Aug. 3 deadline. Despite that rough opening, the team went 29-17 in the last 46 games entering Wednesday’s finale.

Skubal has anchored the Tigers’ rotation since 2024, and his value is undeniable. Back-to-back Cy Young awards and leading the AL in ERA for two straight seasons define his recent run. With Skubal, Detroit made the playoffs, proving he’s a franchise player. Yet trade rumors have swirled all season after he failed to sign an extension last offseason. Teams feel urgency to act now because he hits free agency after the 2026 season.

Contenders like the Dodgers and Brewers have been linked to Skubal as potential suitors. The front office faces a brutal choice: build for the future or cash in on a star. Per NY Post Sports, the situation remains fluid as the deadline approaches. Great pitchers rarely stay in rebuilding zones forever. That standing ovation signaled respect from a fanbase aware they might lose him soon. Every pitch he throws now carries extra weight because the clock is ticking.

Reaching 1,000 strikeouts is huge for any pitcher, but hitting that mark while facing a trade deadline shifts the narrative entirely. It proves Skubal isn’t just a number on a stat sheet; he’s a leader who commands attention. The Tigers built a strong team around him recently, but early-season struggles created a surplus of talent. That surplus forces management to look at the big picture, which usually means moving assets. The 29-17 run in the last 46 games proves the team can compete, but the core might shift.

Fans hate watching a homegrown star potentially leave. He’s been the face of the pitching staff, and losing him would leave a massive hole. The trade market for a pitcher of his caliber is incredibly competitive right now. Teams will offer significant packages to secure his services. Detroit must decide if they want to compete now or rebuild for later. The answer depends on how much they value his remaining contract control. His performance on Wednesday was a stark reminder of exactly what they would be giving up.

Fans need to watch the trade deadline closely as the clock winds down. Skubal’s future is uncertain, but his impact on the game is crystal clear. The Dodgers and Brewers will likely make aggressive moves if the Tigers decide to listen to offers. If he stays, Detroit has a shot to contend again in 2026. If he goes, they’ll need to find a new anchor for their rotation. That standing ovation on Wednesday was a fitting tribute to his first 1,000 strikeouts.

title: 2026 AIG Women's Open storylines: Can Nelly Korda or Haeran Ryu make history?
description: Nelly Korda and Haeran Ryu look to cap off a dominant LPGA season at the 2026 AIG Women's Open in England.
fullText:
When American golfer Nelly Korda blew out her birthday candles on Tuesday evening in celebration of her 28th birthday, she likely wished for one thing: To win the 2026 AIG Women's Open and complete a career grand slam.

The 2026 AIG Women's Open, the fifth and final major of the LPGA calendar year, is set to tee off at the Royal Lytham & St Annes Golf Club in England on Thursday, July 30. The first four majors of the year have been split between two golfers after Korda won the first two and South Korea's Haeran Ryu claimed the last two.

Will Korda or Ryu strike again? Or can someone else win big this year?

Korda and Ryu are vying to become just the fifth woman to win three majors in a single year. American Babe Zaharias was the first woman to do so in 1950, while South Korea's Inbee Park was the last to accomplish the feat in 2013.

"That's always the goal, right? To contend in major championships," Korda said during her preview press conference on Wednesday, July 29. "My attitude this week is control what you can control. Sometimes with golf, you can kind of get pretty agitated with the bounces that you get. ... I think what I've learned is I just need to take a step back and hit the reset button sometimes."

Korda got off to a hot start this year and won the first two LPGA major championships —  the Chevron Championship in April and U.S. Women’s Open in June — to claim the third and fourth major titles of her career. However, Korda's short game failed her at the Women's PGA Championship and she finished tied for eighth place. The championship went to Ryu, the first major of her career after becoming the first player since 1964 to overcome a first-round deficit of at least 10 strokes.

It didn't take Ryu long to capture her second major. She entered the 2026 LPGA Amundi Evian Championship earlier this month in France feeling "more free" after her breakthrough win, admitting that competing felt "less stressful" now. Ryu went on to win the Evian Championship in a playoff against Brooke Henderson to claim back-to-back majors.

Meanwhile, Korda missed the cut at the 2026 Evian Championship after finishing one stroke above the cut line, ending a 34-tournament cut streak dating back to 2024. However, she expects to bounce back quickly.

"It's golf. Just because you're playing well doesn't mean you're invincible and you're going to make every cut and you're going to be in the top 10 every single week," Korda said on Wednesday. "There's going to be weeks that you just don't have it and that's the reality of it. And I feel like I've done this long enough where I've missed enough cuts that it's just about the bounce back."

Korda and Ryu will be paired together in a marquee group during the first two rounds, alongside New Zealand's Lydia Ko, the 2024 AIG Women's Open champion. They are set to tee off at 3:42 a.m. ET on Thursday.

Marquee groups 👀

For round one you'll be able to watch these players live in our early window coverage, available on R&A TV and across selected broadcasters worldwide 💙 pic.twitter.com/7Y2fvNSx6c

— AIG Women’s Open (@AIGWomensOpen) July 28, 2026

With a win, Korda would also complete the career grand slam and have played her way into LPGA Hall of Fame eligibility at the age of 28. Both haven't been accomplished by an American woman since Juli Inkster in 1999.

To qualify for the LPGA Hall of Fame, players must accumulate 27 points by way of winning LPGA tournaments (one point), season-ending awards (one point), an Olympic gold medal (one point) or a major (two points).

Korda currently sits at 25 LPGA Hall of Fame points, not that she knows. The 2020 Olympic champion prefers it that way, previously saying she doesn't want to know how many points she needs. (The answer is two points.)

She finished in 36th place at last year's Women's Open at the Royal Porthcawl Gold Club in the United Kingdom, with her best finish coming in 2024 (No. 2). The last time the Women's Open was contested at the Royal Lytham & St Annes Golf Club in 2018, Korda finished in 42nd place.

The 2026 AIG Women's Open marks the third major tournament in five weeks, which Korda said has taken a toll on her mentally and physically.

"Sometimes with it being the fifth major and coming off of a lot of condensed majors in a packed schedule, I feel like you're a little bit more on edge because you've been in these high pressure moments throughout this middle part of year," Korda, the World No. 1, said Wednesday. "We're coming off of a big part in our season. So I always feel like maybe I'm a little bit more tired, so the bad bounces get to me a little bit mentally."

Head inside the ropes for the final practice session ahead of round one of the AIG Women's Open 💙

Watch here: https://t.co/LIBwp2aK2f@Mastercard | #InsidetheAIGWomensOpen pic.twitter.com/0N9r2B42l5

— AIG Women’s Open (@AIGWomensOpen) July 29, 2026

The last time the Women's Open was staged at Royal Lytham in 2018, English golfer Georgia Hall won her first and only major. Can another British golfer win on home soil? Charley Hull could be the one to break through.

Hull is vying for her maiden major title and has come painfully close numerous times, finishing as a runner-up at the Women's Open in 2023 and 2025. She's finished in second place at a major three other times, including the 2026 U.S. Women's Open that Korda went on to win earlier this year.

"I just want to get over the line and win my first major,” Hull said. "Five second-place finishes in majors kind of hurts."

Korda said it would be "great for the game of golf" if Hull was able to win it all at home.

"She's an amazing player, a funny personality for sure. I enjoy playing with her at anytime," Korda said. "That's sometimes how she goes. It's about putting yourself into that position. You can't control what others are doing, but she's doing something right to always kind of be there, be relevant, be in the hunt. ... You can't get discouraged, it has to be encouraging."

Hall is also set to compete at the 2026 Women's Open, just five months after giving birth to her son.

The 2026 AIG Women's Open, the fifth and final major of the calendar year, is set to tee off on Thursday, July 30, beginning at 1:30 a.m. ET at Royal Lytham & St Annes Golf Club in Lancashire, England.

The CBF is considering the possibility of holding a farewell match for Neymar with the Brazilian National Team.

According to information published by newspaper O Globo this Wednesday (29), however, the idea is still in its early stages.

The federation was contacted and acknowledged that it could organize a farewell match for the player, but pointed out that nothing is planned at the moment because he is still active.

This Tuesday (28), Neymar said in an interview after Santos' Copa Sudamericana match that he has already closed his chapter with the Brazilian National Team.

My time with the National Team is over. I made history, I was very happy, I gave my blood, my life, I always fought and battled for the Yellow Jersey, but now I don't want to anymore

Brazil's No. 10 at the last World Cup had already indicated that he would no longer play for the National Team shortly after the elimination against Norway.

Neymar has a contract with Santos until the end of this year and faces uncertainty over what the next step in his career will be.

title: Saints defensive tackle Bryan Bresee injures knee in opening camp practice
description: New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Bryan Bresee left the opening practice of training camp with a non-contact knee injury that “doesn't look good,” coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday night.  The severity of the injury to Bresee, a first-round draft choice out of Clemson in 2023, was not initially apparent on the field, Moore said.  “It took a little bit I think for him to realize what it felt like,” Moore said.
fullText:
METAIRIE, La. (AP) — New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Bryan Bresee left the opening practice of training camp with a non-contact knee injury that “doesn't look good,” coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday night.

“No one kind of ran into each other, no one fell on anyone. It was just kind of a goofy deal where obviously something unfortunately happened," Moore said during an interview on WWL radio in New Orleans. “It's a tough one.”

The severity of the injury to Bresee, a first-round draft choice out of Clemson in 2023, was not initially apparent on the field, Moore said.

“It took a little bit I think for him to realize what it felt like,” Moore said. "It felt like a little bit of something and then once they checked it out — obviously, we’ll continue to finalize all that — but it doesn’t look great.”

Injuries to knee ligaments can be season-ending, but the Saints have yet to confirm the extent of Bresee's injury.

Bresee has missed just two of the first 51 games of his career, during which he's had 14 1/2 sacks. He also has blocked two field goal attempts.

His absence, if prolonged, could hasten the Saints' reliance on rookie interior defensive linemen Christen Miller second-round draft choice out of Georgia, and Vernon Broughton, a 2025 third-round draft choice out of Texas who spent his rookie season on injured reserve.

“We obviously have to have other guys presented opportunities and certainly those guys will have to take advantage of that,” Moore said. “Bryan will do everything he can to recover and come back as strong as he possibly can.”

title: Lots of optimism as NC State football hits the practice field
description: Head coach Dave Doeren said he was excited about this year's Wolfpack squad and the emergence of QB CJ Bailey as a team leader.
fullText:
NC State officially opened its 2026 football season on Wednesday with the first day of fall camp.

Dave Doeren, the Wolfpack's long-tenured head coach, is entering his 14th season and still chasing his first ACC championship.

Doeren said he was excited about this year's squad.

"I feel great. I got to tell you, it's so fun to be on the field today," Doeren said. "I'm not going to say that I'm comfortable because first day, you're all excited to get out there and all that, but like, there's a lot of good things going on right now."

NC State Head Coach Dave Doeren has good feelings for the program going into the season. @ABC11_WTVD pic.twitter.com/YWYwVKU9lL

— ABC11Charlie Mickens (@GameDayCharlie) July 29, 2026

Reflecting on his time in Raleigh, Doeren said, "I think it's not so many the years that you do it, it's the teams you do it with."

One reason for optimism this fall is the return of quarterback CJ Bailey, who is back for a third season.

Football season is officially here.

First stop— NC State. 🐺🩸

Year 14 for Dave Doeren, behind QB1 CJ Bailey.

I just asked Bailey about the Wolfpack being picked 7th in the ACC preseason poll…his response?

“Fuel to the fire.” 👀 @ABC11_WTVD pic.twitter.com/5k2fuipbfw

— Travon Miles (@TrayABC11) July 29, 2026

Doeren said Bailey was an offensive leader last season, but now he's developing into a team leader.

It's a role that Bailey is ready to embrace.

"The past couple of years, I was learning, learning from other leaders," Bailey said. "Those NFL guys helping me, teaching me how to lead, and you know, just practicing it, speaking a lot, using my voice, stepping out in front has just prepared me for this moment."

"Just adds fuel to the fire." NC State QB CJ Bailey isn't concerned about the Wolfpack's predicted seventh-place finish. pic.twitter.com/CjXp9rw9Hh

— ABC11 EyewitnessNews (@ABC11_WTVD) July 29, 2026

The Wolfpack was picked to finish seventh in the ACC according to the media's preseason poll.

Bailey was undaunted by the news.

"That's actually a good fact. I really didn't know about that, but it just adds fuel to the fire for sure," Bailey said. "Like, we'll just stay motivated. Like, every little thing motivates us.

"I want to win every game and prove everybody wrong," he added.

The Wolfpack opens the season on Aug. 29 at Virginia, a game that was supposed to be played in Brazil but was later moved to Charlottesville.

title: De Zerbi wants Bergvall at Spurs, but can't promise starting role
description: Roberto De Zerbi said he wants in-demand midfielder Lucas Bergvall to stay at Tottenham, but cannot guarantee  the Sweden World Cup player a starting role."I can't give, for any player in the world, a place in the first XI guaranteed."
fullText:
Roberto De Zerbi said he wants in-demand midfielder Lucas Bergvall to stay at Tottenham, but cannot guarantee  the Sweden World Cup player a starting role.

The 20-year-old reportedly wants to leave with interest from Newcastle and Nottingham Forest.

His future was cast into doubt by the recent arrivals of club-record signings Matheus Fernandes from West Ham and Sandro Tonali from Newcastle.

Spurs manager De Zerbi denied Bergvall had told him he was looking for an exit after starting him in the pre-season friendly against Sydney FC on Wednesday.

Tottenham won 4-2 on penalties after the match finished 1-1.

"I'm always being very clear with him and with you. I would like that he stays with us," De Zerbi said.

"I think he's potentially a top, top, player. But then I don't want to convince anyone to stay.

"Tottenham is already, without me, a top club and we are not to convince anyone to stay.

"I can't give, for any player in the world, a place in the first XI guaranteed."

French striker Mathys Tel scored a stunning free-kick to put Spurs 1-0 ahead  at half-time against Sydney, but they failed to capitalise and the hosts' new Japanese signing Takahiro Sekine levelled.

Tottenham's shootout win came after a 2-0 victory over Auckland FC on Sunday as they build towards their English Premier League opener against Brentford on August 22.

"I think we played well, especially in the first half," he said.

"In the second half, we changed many players, but good quality of play, good performances and I think we are working very well with the younger players."

Tonali missed Tottenham's first tour game with a niggle, but played the entire second-half, while fellow new recruit Andy Robertson was given a 25-minute debut.

But there was no appearance from Fernandes, whose absence De Zerbi attributed to "just fatigue, in the calf, and also for him, we took the decision not to take any risks".

The Italian manager suggested Fernandes would also miss Tottenham's final tour match against Chelsea in Sydney on Saturday.

James Maddison was another absentee along with Kevin Danso, Destiny Udogie, Micky van de Ven, Jan Paul van Hecke and Dominic Solanke.

"Danso, van de Ven, Solanke, Jan Paul van Hecke, I thought they were not ready yet to play without risk," De Zerbi said.

"Maybe some of them can play the next game, on Saturday against Chelsea. Maybe not in the beginning, maybe at the beginning Robertson and Sandro Tonali.

"It is about managing the players. I wouldn't like to take any risks."

title: Sahana Chokshi of Jacksonville moves up in second round of Junior PGA
description: Sahana Chokshi of Jacksonville leads area players in the Junior PGA Championship, in Frisco, Texas.
fullText:
Sahana Chokshi of Jacksonville made four birdies on her way to a 71 on July 29, and through 36 holes is tied for 11th at 3-under-par 141 in the Junior PGA Championship at Fields Ranch at PGA Frisco East Course in Frisco, Texas.

Chokshi, a rising senior at Episcopal who shot 70 in the first round at the West Course, is six shots behind leader Alexa Takai of Honolulu (66). Lily Wachter of St. Augustine, who had a 68 in the first round, had three birdies, four bogeys and a double bogey on her way to a 75, and fell from a tie for fifth to a tie for 20th at 1-under 143.

Sofia Rivera of St. Augustine shot 73 and missed the cut to the low 60 players, plus ties, at 5-over 149.

After a first-round 75 at the East Course, Charlie Woods was in danger of missing the 36-hole cut. However, he birdied his first hole (No. 9) at the West Course and shot 70 to finish at 1-over 145 and in a tie for 46th.

Woods birdied Nos. 18 and 2, bogeyed the third hole, then parred his last five. He tied for ninth in last year's Junior PGA at the Purdue University golf course, after entering the final day in a tie for second.

There is a 54-hole cut to the low-30 players, plus ties, after the third round on July 30.

title: EA Sports reveal Madden '27 player ratings. Where do the 49ers rank?
description: Check out the San Francisco 49ers player ratings on EA Sports' Madden NFL 27. See which players were given a 99 rating and who weren't.
fullText:
The release of EA Sports' Madden NFL 27 means that we're that much closer to football season. The video game will be made available Aug. 13 with pre-orders are available and early access on Aug. 6 and 10.

EA Sports released its player ratings Wednesday and this is where the football world really gets to chirping. It's where the talks of bragging rights for who's the best player really get brewing between the athletes and fans alike.

Six players had a 99 rating, but none of them were members of the San Francisco 49ers. Instead the 49ers' division rivals, the Los Angeles Rams, had a couple players atop the list as quarterback Matthew Stafford and newly acquired edge rusher Myles Garrett were given 99 ratings. The other signal caller in the league to be rated 99 is Buffalo Bills' Josh Allen.

Making the 99 list was Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. He is the top-rated receiver in NFC, according to Madden NFL 27. Cincinnati Bengals receiver Jamarr Chase is only other wideout with a 99 rating.

Madden NFL 27 says that Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride is the best at his position, giving him a 99 rating.

Although there weren't any 49ers players rated 99, they still have some of the best players in the league, according to their Madden ratings. Here's a look at the San Francisco 49ers player ratings and leading attributes.

The 49ers might not have a player with a 99 preseason rating, but some are pretty close. A good start to the season and they could progress to a 99 easily.

San Francisco running back Christian McCaffrey has a 97 rating. Some of his attribute ratings include a 90 speed, 93 agility and 99 awareness. He's rated the second-best tailback in the league behind the Detroit Lions' 98-rated Jahmyr Gibbs.

McBride is considered the best tight end in the league, but don't forget about George Kittle. Although coming off of a torn right Achilles, Kittle is still considered the second-best tight end in football with a 96 rating. Kittle has a 77 run block rating and a 78 impact blocking rating. He possesses some of the best hands with a 94 catching, 89 spectacular catch and 89 catch in traffic ratings.

Trent Williams is still considered one of the best at his position. The left tackle has a 96 rating. He's tied with Denver Broncos' Garett Bolles, and both are a couple ratings behind Detroit Lions' Penei Sewell, who has a 98 rating.

Veteran wide receiver Mike Evans is still given his props. Madden NFL 27 gave Evans a 91 rating with attributes including 97 jumping, 97 catch in traffic, 96 spectacular catch and 93 catching.

A player rating for 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy was not yet available on the EA Sports website.

49ers linebacker Fred Warner did not have a player rating available on the EA Sports website.

The 2026 NFL Draft class has its ratings released as well. Here's how the 49ers' rookie ratings look for Madden NFL 27.

de to improve the defense this year after just one day of training camp.

The seventh-year quarterback doesn't know yet how much work he will get in preseason games against an actual opponent, but the Bengals' defensive line looks to provide a different kind of test with 6-foot-5, 350-pound Dexter Lawrence lining up inside.

That's a new challenge he welcomes as he tries to prepare for imposing defensive lines he will face during the regular season.

"The D-Line, certainly, size difference from last year is the most glaring thing," Burrow said after the first practice Wednesday. "The pocket was a little different today. Tough to tell when you don't have pads, but I'm excited to see what those guys can do."

Lawrence said he looked Burrow "in the eyes a couple times but didn't say much." He looks forward to competing with Burrow in camp as Lawrence tries to get pressure on him and Burrow tries to evade that.

Burrow said it's good practice being forced to get the ball out quickly.

"He got back there pretty quick a couple of times," Burrow said. "We're going to have to get that thing out. Made some blind throws today because of how big he is. And he pushes that pocket and gets close to you. You have to be able to throw without seeing. I think it's great for the games, but that's a challenge. That's going to be a big part of our team this year. I'm excited to watch it."

Seeing Lawrence coming at him in 11-on-11 drills was a nice reminder to Burrow of the investments Cincinnati made into the roster this offseason to try to reach goals of getting back to the playoffs.

Burrow wants to see the team maximize the opportunities in front of them with a loaded offense and a lot of work put into improving the defense.

title: Justin Herbert sets the tone as Chargers open training camp with renewed expectations
description: EL SEGUNDO, Calif.
fullText:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. — Under clear blue skies and in front of thousands of Chargers fans packed into The Bolt on Wednesday morning, the Los Angeles Chargers officially opened training camp with a fresh sense of optimism.

The memory of last January still lingers.

The Chargers' 2025 season came to a disappointing end in the Wild Card Round with a 16-3 loss to the New England Patriots, a game in which quarterback Justin Herbert failed to throw a touchdown pass. The defeat dropped Herbert to 0-3 in the postseason, adding another chapter to the criticism surrounding one of the league's most gifted quarterbacks.

Now begins another season, and another opportunity.

For this franchise, everything starts with No. 10.

Jessica Cryderman - The Sporting Tribune

Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) greeting running back Omarion Hampton (8) during Chargers training camp at the Bolt on Wednesday, July 29th in El Segundo, CA.

Wherever Herbert goes, the Chargers go.

"I think there's always a sense of urgency," Herbert said following Wednesday's practice. "I think the guys are focused and dialed in this year."

It was Herbert's first football practice since January, and he looked every bit like a quarterback eager to turn the page. Working in the offense's new shotgun alignment, Herbert appeared comfortable throughout the session. His footwork was clean, his timing sharp, and he consistently delivered accurate throws across the field.

Take a close look at Chargers QB Justin Herbert on his first day of Training Camp, who recently proposed to Madison Beer. @SportingTrib | #BoltUp pic.twitter.com/TzXyncwsJL

— Fredo Cervantes (@FredoCervantes) July 29, 2026

One noticeable improvement came from the work Herbert put in over the offseason.

"You just get to the point where you're not thinking about it," Herbert said of refining his footwork. "As opposed to months ago it was making sure your feet were lined up with the routes, timing."

That development could prove significant with one of the biggest additions of the Chargers' offseason now calling plays.

Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel has already made an impression on his new quarterback.

"He loves what he does. He loves football, he loves being here," Herbert said. "It makes everyone want to work harder for him. We're really fortunate to play for him."

"I could tell we were going to get along early on."

The pairing of Herbert's elite arm talent with McDaniel's creative offensive mind has quickly become one of the NFL's most intriguing storylines entering the season. Expectations inside the organization, and among the fan base, have risen accordingly.

Whether Herbert will see preseason action remains undecided.

"I don't know. Coach Harbaugh would have a better feel for that," Herbert said. "I'm not opposed."

Herbert played one drive during last year's preseason against the Rams, and Jim Harbaugh has yet to reveal his plans for August.

While football dominated the day, Herbert also shared a lighter moment.

Just days after announcing his engagement to pop star Madison Beer, Herbert was asked whether proposing or making his first NFL start created more nerves.

"The proposal, for sure," Herbert said with a smile.

Congrats to Justin Herbert and Madison Beer on their engagement ❤️ (via madisonbeer/IG) pic.twitter.com/Ot1aGhXsFU

He joked that he had significantly more time to prepare for the proposal than his unexpected NFL debut in 2020 after Tyrod Taylor was ruled inactive minutes before the game.

Harbaugh couldn't resist joining in.

"Awesome. Feel great for him," Harbaugh said before noting that Valentine's Day next year falls on the same day as Super Bowl LX at SoFi Stadium.

"Valentine's Day. SoFi,” Harbaugh said. “Little hairs on your arms start standing up."

For Herbert, the offseason brought a major personal milestone.

Now his focus shifts entirely back to football.

Day 1 of training camp is only the beginning, but Herbert looked every bit like a quarterback ready to embrace the challenge ahead. Comfortable in a new offense, energized by a fresh coaching voice, and surrounded by heightened expectations, the Chargers will once again go as far as their franchise quarterback can take them.

After another playoff disappointment, the mission is clear.

Herbert doesn't just have to play well. He has to lead the Chargers where they haven't been able to go.

Training camp is underway, and with Herbert at the controls, a new chapter has officially begun.

title: Paige Bueckers, Angel Reese go at each other in intense Wings-Dream battle
description: Intense start to the game between the Wings and the Dream, with the two stars.
fullText:
Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese brought some extra intensity to Wednesday night’s matchup between the Dallas Wings and Atlanta Dream.

Two of the WNBA’s biggest young stars found themselves matched up during the first half at College Park Center, and neither was willing to back down. Bueckers attempted to drive past Reese before the Dream forward used her strength to cut off the lane.

That led to a physical back-and-forth battle as Bueckers continued trying to create space. The Wings guard eventually lost control of the ball, but the whistle had already blown for a foul on Reese.

The sequence quickly drew attention on social media.

“Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese are going at it,” Underdog WNBA wrote while sharing a clip of the matchup.

Bueckers and Reese are friendly away from the court, but there was no room for pleasantries once the ball went up Wednesday. Their entertaining individual battle added another layer to an important game between two teams near the top of the WNBA standings.

The matchup came just days after Bueckers and Reese spent time together during WNBA All-Star Weekend in Chicago. They even discussed making a friendly wager on Wednesday’s game, although Bueckers jokingly appeared to forget about it when asked before tipoff.

Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese are going at itpic.twitter.com/djYWjzzX9d

— Underdog WNBA (@UnderdogWNBA) July 30, 2026

Once the game started, however, both players quickly shifted back into competitive mode. Dallas entered Wednesday with an 18-9 record and sat fourth in the Western Conference. Atlanta arrived at 16-10 while riding a three-game winning streak and holding second place in the Eastern Conference.

The Wings also had revenge on their minds. Atlanta won each of the first two meetings between the teams this season, including a 77-72 victory at College Park Center on May 12. Reese dominated the glass in that game, finishing with 12 points and 16 rebounds. Bueckers scored 15 points for Dallas, but the Wings shot just 4-of-26 from beyond the arc.

The second meeting was far less competitive, with Atlanta earning an 86-69 home victory on May 22. Dallas appeared determined to change the script in the third meeting. The Wings took a 38-32 advantage into halftime after outscoring the Dream 22-16 during the second quarter.

MORE: Lexie Hull steals spotlight with glamorous pregame look before Fever victory

Bueckers entered Wednesday averaging 20.9 points per game, the sixth-best mark in the WNBA. After winning Rookie of the Year in 2025, the former UConn star has quickly developed into the centerpiece of a Dallas team that has emerged as a legitimate contender. Reese has enjoyed an impressive first season with Atlanta after being traded by the Chicago Sky in April. Her rebounding, physicality and improving offensive game have helped the Dream climb near the top of the Eastern Conference.

The two stars took very different paths to the WNBA, but both have become must-watch players capable of producing viral moments whenever they share the court. Wednesday’s physical exchange was the latest example. Bueckers and Reese might be friends before and after the game, but their battle made one thing perfectly clear: Neither one plans to give the other an inch between the lines.

fullText:
The Minnesota Vikings start training camp this week and there are a bunch of news items that have coincided with that this week worth addressing. As a reminder, rookies and quarterbacks reported on Sunday, while veterans reported on Tuesday. Wednesday’s practice included the first press conferences of training camp.

The Vikings acquired linebacker/safety Jamal Adams this week. Adams is a former 6th overall pick and Pro Bowler who has since had injury issues and bounced around a couple teams in recent years, including Seattle from 2020-2023 where he got to know Vikings’ GM Nolan Teasley. That relationship seemed to be a factor in his signing with the Vikings from his comments about the signing on Wednesday, but he’s also a good fit for Brian Flores’ scheme as a versatile defender.

Jamal Adams on Decision to Sign with Vikings, Respect for Brian Flores, … https://t.co/dQt5XkSVJ1 via @YouTube

— Warren Ludford (@wludford) July 30, 2026

He played around 450 snaps last season with the Raiders at linebacker (Adams was a safety previously) and was an above-average performer according to PFF. He’s listed on the Vikings’ website at 6’1”, 213 pounds- which is light for a linebacker. He looks a bit heavier than that though.

He signed a league minimum deal last year with the Raiders and I wouldn’t be surprised if he signed a similar deal with the Vikings, although the terms of his contract have not yet been released. But I expect him to make the roster as a linebacker. I could see him replacing Josh Metellus’ reps in that role last season and also reducing some reps for Eric Wilson. After watching Adams’ tape last year at linebacker with the Raiders, my first impression is that he’s a decent linebacker. He may be the best option in coverage among linebackers on the roster. He is also very good at reading plays and always has his eyes in the backfield. He was either a hook zone or flat defender in coverage last season and he showed good awareness in that role. Occasionally he’d run with receivers, whether backs or tight ends or wide receivers and did alright in that role too, but he’s not a good matchup against top wide receivers to be sure. As a run defender, he’s not afraid of contact but sometimes he will be the sacrificial defender to absorb blocks or clog up one hole for others to make the tackle instead of trying to make the tackle himself. He doesn’t show the ability to shed blocks like a traditional linebacker, but he can work his way through the trash, as they say, to make a tackle. As a pass rusher he did okay but could improve by taking more direct routes to the quarterback and improving his ability to get by chip blockers. He’s not a blow-em-up blitzer when it comes to taking on running back blockers like Blake Cashman or Ivan Pace or Eric Wilson have been. He blitzes like a safety.

Vikings’ defensive coordinator Brian Flores talked about Adams in his Wednesday press conference saying that Adams is a real football guy and that his role will be determined by what he can do well and be productive at. I’d be surprised if he played anything but linebacker, however, although you could say he’s a bit of a hybrid linebacker/strong safety. But I expect him to make the roster and play around half the defensive snaps, maybe more if there are injuries. His acquisition is good insurance against injury in the linebacker group, which is a significant risk with Blake Cashman having missed a few games every season that last few years and Eric Wilson at age 32. His role could decrease potentially if Jake Golday is able to ramp up over the course of the season. He could also end up playing more snaps than Eric Wilson if they lean on him 

No surprise that the Vikings got a deal done extending Brian O’Neill prior to the start of training camp. That seemed like it was in the cards all summer. It was a well-deserved extension for O’Neill, who has been a captain and core player for many years now and one of the better right tackles in the league. It’s a four-year, $96 million deal ($24 million AAV) but further details have not yet become available. The length of the extension goes through O’Neill’s age 35, which makes it likely that O’Neill begins and ends his career in Minnesota. I wouldn’t be surprised if the deal was structured in such a way that the Vikings could pull out a year early without a big dead cap hit, but at this point O’Neill has not shown any signs of reduced performance. It varies by player, but some tackles can continue playing at a high level well into their 30s. But extending O’Neill means the Vikings will have their bookend tackles for four more seasons- Christian Darrisaw is signed through 2029 and O’Neill now through 2030.

Vikings defensive backs coach Gerald Alexander was suspended for three weeks without pay for a DUI incident back in April. Terrible timing for a coach to serve a suspension for the first three weeks of training camp. Apparently defensive coordinator Brian Flores stepped in to coach the defensive backs at the beginning of Wednesday’s practice. Not sure what the plan is for the whole three weeks, but not a good time for a coach to miss.

Harrison Smith’s name was brought up on a couple occasions during Tuesday’s press conferences and judging by the comments from Kevin O’Connell it doesn’t appear that Smith signing on for another season is imminent nor do those discussions appear to be ramping up. I’d be surprised at this point if Smith came back before the start of the regular season, if he does at all.

Kyler Murray took the first reps with the first team in team drills and alternated with J.J. McCarthy every four reps with Murray ultimately getting 16 reps to McCarthy’s 12, although I’ve seen slightly different rep counts. Kevin O’Connell said that reps between the two would not always be perfectly even every day for a variety of reasons, but the initial intension is to split reps roughly evenly between the two quarterbacks.

Will have 

— Kevin Seifert (@SeifertESPN) July 29, 2026

There doesn’t appear to be a clear winner of the day between the two quarterbacks according to reporters attending the practice. Some nice throws and misses by both quarterbacks.

StarTribune reported an even split in reps: “Murray and quarterback J.J. McCarthy split first-team reps. Murray took the lead in two 11-on-11 periods and one 7-on-7 period within a roughly 90-minute practice. Both quarterbacks worked with the first- and second-team offenses, ending with an even split of total snaps: 16 each in full-team drills and another six snaps each in a 7-on-7 passing drill. It’s a work in progress. Neither quarterback connected consistently with receiver Justin Jefferson, who watched Murray miss him on a deep ball down the sideline and McCarthy throw a late pass over the middle deflected by safety Jay Ward. Jefferson finally caught a pass in team drills when Murray found him over safety Josh Metellus during Murray’s penultimate 11-on-11 rep. title: Cincinnati Bengals: Shemar Stewart injured, fight breaks out on Day 1 of camp
description: Jul. 29—Cincinnati Bengals coach Zac Taylor said his message to the team before the first practice of training camp was about getting the work in while also "trying to protect your teammates." By the time the Bengals got into team drills Wednesday, July 29, that message was already being put to the test. Just a few minutes after defensive end Shemar Stewart needed to be carted off after ...
fullText:
Jul. 29—Cincinnati Bengals coach Zac Taylor said his message to the team before the first practice of training camp was about getting the work in while also "trying to protect your teammates."

Just a few minutes after defensive end Shemar Stewart needed to be carted off after hyperextending his left knee on a routine team rep against Cody Ford, a scuffle broke out.

A closed fist swung at Ja'Marr Chase after a first-team 11-on-11 rep, and Chase ended up ripping off the helmet of DJ Turner and forcefully rolling it on the ground about 20 yards away. As players from both offense and defense came together in a scrum, Chase came out of it jawing at Jalen Davis.

Turner said it was "just competing" and "nothing else to it." Davis liked seeing that kind of chippy behavior on Day 1 and hopes the intensity keeps up throughout camp.

"I always feel like the energy got to be like that. It got to be like that on both sides of the field. I hope it's a fight every day...to get the energy going. Like I said, we just competing, and that's it."

Tee Higgins got right in the middle of the scrum, trying to play peacekeeper, and said he was just trying to protect his "guy." He didn't mind the extra edge on display but didn't want to let it get out of hand.

Davis was on the sideline for the next series, while Ja'Sir Taylor jumped in with the first-team defense, but Joe Burrow went right toward Turner on the following two passes, one to Chase and one to Higgins. Burrow smiled when asked about whether it was intentional to target Turner after the scuffle and said "you'll never know."

Chase was still talking to Davis as players moved onto the next drill, but they eventually shook hands. Davis said the players still love one another, despite any bad blood that might appear on the field. The defense especially wants to set a different tone this year, as that side of the ball seeks to show the past struggles are in the past.

"We just want to come out and just have a different mentality, and that's what came out," Davis said.

There's a fine line between competitiveness and putting teammates at risk of injury, though. Players didn't feel like anything went overboard Wednesday, and Stewart's injury was just a routine play.

Davis, Turner and Dexter Lawrence all said they didn't even realize Stewart had gone down, but were disappointed to hear about it later. He was carted off right before the altercation, and there was no update after practice.

Stewart missed nine games in his rookie season due to a pair of injuries last year, and he was hopeful to be able to make a bigger impact in Year 2.

The Bengals are anxious to get back on track this season, and that takes everyone being invested, Turner said. That's why he, Dax Hill and Chase Brown are still showing up on time and practicing, despite not having long-term deals in place. All three players are in the final season of their contract, including Hill playing on a fifth-year option.

Everyone was at practice on Day 1.

"In my situation I am right now, I'm just locked into my craft right now," Turner said. "Honestly, we have to win this year, and so me being out there is really important to the team."

Cleveland Browns cornerback Denzel Ward became the highest-paid defensive back in NFL history for the second time in his career on Tuesday when he signed a two-year, $62.2 million extension, including $52.3 million in guaranteed money. That could help drive up the price for everyone else, but Turner said it was deserved for Ward.

"That was big," Turner said. "Like I said, Denzel was the top corner, though, so that's not surprising at all.

Hill said it wasn't a question whether he would show up or not. He also has an important role to play in the Cincinnati secondary this year.

Despite speculation the Bengals might move Hill back inside after drafting Tacario Davis in the third round, they are keeping Hill outside, as he had hoped would be the case.

"I mean it's kind of just reassuring," Hill said after expressing the importance of staying in one position this spring after moving from safety to nickel to outside in his first four seasons. "I mean, I know I can play the position, so just hearing that, you know, just kind of reassures things."

selected target.

title: OpenMetaHarness
description: A one-file bootloader that helps coding agents execute long-horizon projects across sessions and context windows. - openmetaharness/openmetaharness
fullText:
Coding agents have become highly capable, but they can be unreliable on long-horizon,
evolving projects that unfold across many context windows.

OpenMetaHarness is a cognitive architecture that enables coding agents to develop and
execute on a long-horizon project vision from 0 to 1 with minimal human
intervention and maximum token efficiency across multiple sessions and context
windows.

You will be able to direct a persistent engineering operation whose memory, judgment,
and discipline compound with the project. As the project accumulates verified
decisions, operating lessons, and category-specific trust, any compatible coding agent
can resume with more context, repeat fewer mistakes, and work autonomously for longer
stretches.

Create a new directory, put openmetaharness.md inside it, and
open your coding agent in that directory. Then type:

That's it. The bootloader sets up the project, starts the harness, and you are ready to
build.

OpenMetaHarness is distributed as a plain-text Markdown file so its instructions can be
read directly, searched, diffed, and reviewed without executing macros or unpacking an
opaque binary format. Markdown alone cannot prevent invisible Unicode characters, so
the validator also rejects zero-width characters, bidirectional text controls,
non-breaking spaces, soft hyphens, and unsafe control characters in harness files.
Suspicious text is never normalized silently; validation stops and identifies the file,
line, and code point.

The bootloader has six sequential phases. The lifecycle tables describe what happens
and in what order. The module map that follows describes the persistent control system
that operates across those phases.

These systems are mutually exclusive by responsibility and collectively cover every
mandatory module embedded in the bootloader. Domain artifacts are generated only when
the selected project profile requires them.

I've been working with multimodal agentic systems ever since the ImageNet and DQN
days. It's amazing to see all the progress in the community since then. The way I work
with AI now is exactly what I dreamed of a decade ago.

When I started vibecoding last year, I came up with new ways to set up projects to
avoid known issues in long-horizon task execution. I thought it would be great if I
had one simple file that a coding agent could read when I start a new project to
address these known issues while improving efficiency and autonomy long-term.

OpenMetaHarness has unlocked a better way for me to use AI. It allows me and my
collaborators to run a persistent engineering operation designed to be model and
system-agnostic, whose memory, judgment, and operating discipline compound over
time.

In some of my tests, as the project matured, the loop ran for an hour before needing
human input. When my collaborator started a new session on a new device with a new
coding agent all they had to prompt it with was continue where you left off.

I call this OpenMetaHarness, a one-file bootloader and a README released under the
MIT License. I'd love the community to contribute to this; this is the first version,
and over time we can make it better and better!

Contributions are welcome. Three things are worth knowing before you open a pull
request, because they are easy to get wrong with the best intentions.

The project stays this shape. A README and a one-file bootloader. It will not be
split into modules, grown into a framework, or given a package to install. Changes that
would make it something else are out of scope, however well made.

The bootloader grows rather than shrinks. Improvements add new guidance or clarify
what is already there, instead of deleting or compressing it, so the reasoning behind
earlier decisions stays visible to the agents and people who come later. A change that
tidies the file by cutting it is the most common thing I have to turn down.

The message from the creator is mine. Please leave that section alone. Everything
else in the README is fair game to improve.

Good contributions include a bug with a reproduction, a clarification where two agents
would read the same passage differently, or a new domain profile that composes with the
existing ones. Keep a pull request to one coherent change, and open an issue first if
you are unsure whether something fits.

OpenMetaHarness, the bootloader and README, is MIT-licensed: free to use,
read, fork, and modify.

Projects created with the bootloader are private and proprietary by default. That is a
separate default for your work, and you can override it for any project.

title: Logic for Programmers by Hillel Wayne
description: Practical math for the working programmer.
fullText:
A book about math, software, and using one to fix the other.

Written for the working programmer. No math background required.

227 pages. Ebook includes PDF and EPUB, DRM-free.

This is a book about designing, verifying, and reasoning about software better. And it’s about how learning a little bit of logic, the mathematics of Booleans, unlocks all sorts of cool techniques in our field.

If you want to get a feel for what it’s like, try reading a sample chapter!

Everything in the book is meant to be practical. Early chapters are on topics like “simplifying conditionals” and “ensuring an API change won’t break clients”. Later chapters are on slightly more esoteric subjects, like “finding race conditions in hypothetical software designs” and “minimizing the wall clock time of a distributed task”. Not everything will be useful to everyone, but I hope everyone finds something useful!

Nope! You don’t need to know math besides the Boolean AND, OR, and NOT that programmers pick up through daily experience. The book covers the rest of the math you need.

That said, you do need to know some programming! This book is meant for intermediate-to-advanced programmers and I assume the reader knows universal topics like loops, version control, testing, etc. Some chapters expect more specific knowledge like SQL or API design. Chapters are independent, though, so if something doesn’t fit your needs, go ahead and skip it.

Logicians use the symbols ∀ and ∃ to mean “for all” and “there exists”, respectively. For example, we could write the sentence “everybody has a favorite color” as ∀p ∈ Person: ∃c ∈ Color: IsFavoriteColor(p, c).

To make learning the topics (and searching the book) easier, I use English words instead of math symbols. So the same expression would be all p in People: (some c in Color: IsFavoriteColor(p, c)).

If you want to read the book on your phone or computer, you can get it as a PDF or EPUB. Here’s the PDF:

The print version is identical except with black-and-white printing and wider page margins. You can buy it on Amazon.

Here’s a table of contents and corresponding techniques:

Plus some appendices on math notation, useful rewrite rules, and advanced topics in logic. All code samples are available on GitHub, along with a bunch of extra samples on the same topics that are not used in the book.

It’s just about 50,000 words and a bit over 200 pages. The extra credits add another 4,000 words or so.

There’s a lot of interesting topics that I wanted to cover but couldn’t because they weren’t useful or focused enough to be in the book. So I put them in an extra credit repository with links in the book. This covers stuff like how to calculate the size of a state space, the theory of partial orders, and a few other small things.

title: Manual: •.,:;?·
description: Dots and commas, numbers in English, bullet, interpunct, and operators
fullText:
Quotation marks, braсkets, and various kinds of spaces are a multi-faceted and controversial subject. But apart from those, there are glyphs much more simple in terms of design and use — because of their ubiquity, they mostly fly under the radar. In this article, we continue to talk about basic punctuation characters.

In European and many other languages the period marks the end of a sentence. The symbol is also used for marking initials and abbreviations, and in some regions — as a decimal separator, or a separator of hours and minutes when registering time. Typically, the period is not used in the last sentence of a headline.

Depending on the typeface’s design, the period can be rounded, rectangular, rhomboid, etc. The symbol correlates to the dot above i, but is normally larger.

The period is a frequent symbol, therefore its shape affects the overall intonation of a typeface. The most principled designers can discard an (otherwise high-quality) typeface, if they are not satisfied with its periods.

In some legacy typefaces, the period has asymmetrical sidebearings — in this case, the space after the period would be excessive, you might need to track it. Today, it is customary practice design period with equal sidebearings — because the cases of its use are not limited to traditions.

In monospaced fonts, the period glyph has the same width as all the others — that means very wide sidebearings, which result in the widest space at the end of a sentence. Whether it needs to be compensated or not — that depends on your task.

Quality typefaces have period, comma, and other punctuation kerned, when paired with certain glyphs — to avoid excessive white holes in the setting.

According to typesetting rules in Russian language, initials shall be spaced, however in most cases regular spaces after periods are too much, which is why it is considered good manners to use thin spaces.

In any case, this situation requires a non-breaking space — surname and name should not be separated by line break.

The period is used as a decimal symbol in English language — as well as in the language of former British colonies, in China, Japan, and some other countries.

The period as a decimal separator is the default setting in PCs and other kinds of gadgets, because they originated from the US. In most cases, the American notation system can be changed to a local one, but will keep reminding of itself in code and many UIs.

The period can be used for separating hours and minutes instead of a colon, but it is rather personal preferences or editorial policy than an established practice. For example, in Britain The Guardian writes 13.12, while BBC prefers 13:12. In Russia, the period in indicating time is used by certain online media — for instance, Afisha.Daily uses colon for indicating the time of publication, yet utilises a period between hours and minutes within texts. In some countries (such as Switzerland or Latvia) the period is considered standard and more preferable when registering time.

The comma separates parts of a sentence. In English-speaking countries the comma is used as a thousands separator, while most European countries prefer spaces — and the comma is used as a decimal separator. To avoid miscommunication, do keep in mind these localities.

The comma can be constructed either as a circle with a stroke coming of it — or as one curving or slanted stroke.

In most typefaces, the comma has identical shape to apostrophe and quotation marks. The diacritical comma in Latvian and Romanian often corresponds to the regular comma — that said, diacritics would be significantly smaller. As opposed to diacritical commas, the design of Сzech/Slovak caron
Caron, or háček (ˇ) is a diacritical mark used in Slavic, Baltic, Uralic, and some other languages. In Czech and Slovak narrow letters with ascending elements (l d t L) can also have caron — this situations requires a special form, which is called Czech/Slovak caron. must differ from that of the regular comma and apostrophe. Replacing Сzech/Slovakian caron with an apostrophe is incorrect and misleading.

The ellipsis is a separate glyph consisting of three dots. It is used for indicating omissions, pauses, breaks, or interruptions.

In omissions and lacunae the ellipsis is placed inside brackets, regular or square, or pointy ones — this depends on the typographic tradition.

The ellipsis as a separate glyph can be looser or more condensed than three dots in a row. In certain software, three typeset dots are automatically replaced by one ellipsis — provided the typeface includes this glyph.

The bullet is a graphic marker, while the interpunct is a punctuation mark. Both glyphs are typically designed as vertically centered dots, but they may differ in size and sidebearings.

Normally, the bullet is larger and thicker than a period; it is used to introduce items in a list. The bullet symbol may take a non-dot shape, sometimes it even comes in several options — this depends on the type designer’s preferences. Apart from circular, bullets may be hollow, square, diamond, etc. We recommend looking into the glyph palette to see the entire range of bullets.

The interpunct is typically of the same size as the period, and is placed in the visual middle of the x-height. Depending on language and situation, the interpunct is used for interword separation, as a mathematical symbol, as a part of geminated l
Ela geminada (The geminated l) is written as ŀl and is different in meaning and sound from a simple doubled ll. The typesetting of the geminated l generates debate and discussions: as an integral symbol it has no value in Unicode, while Ldot and ldot do have one. Most frequently the interpunct is used instead of the dot, many type designers create localised features for correct spacing — however, the problem of displaying the integral, not breakable symbol remains. Sometimes the interpunct is replaced by a regular period, placed between the letters on the visual middle, but in certain fonts this option would look too heavy. in Catalan, etc.

Often, an interpunct or a bullet are used for separating parts in a sentence — for example, for separating different languages on one line. In such cases, it doesn’t really matter which glyph you use — as long as it does the job. The interpunct as a separator may look neater, while the bullet would be more visible.

The Unicode table contains several items related to bullets and interpuncts, which scares both designers and font users. In addition to basic Bullet (u+2022), there is also Bullet Operator (u+2219). Apart from regular interpunct Middle Dot (u+00B7), there is Dot Operator (u+22C5) and a number of local variations, such as Greek Ano Teleia (u+0387), and Word Separator Middle Dot (u+2E31). The latter is almost never present in fonts. The Greek Ano Teleia serves as the semicolon, is normally as large as an interpunct, but placed higher — these symbols should not be confused.

The Unicode Consortium recommends using operator glyphs in all math settings. Those may look different: a Bullet Operator might be intended as a multiplication sign, while in other cases it correlates to a regular bullet. Sometimes there is no pattern whatsoever, it all comes down to the decision of a type designer.

In different fonts, availability and shape of these additional symbols differ, while their use is discussed both in type design communities and on other user forums.

In French, the two-piece punctuation glyphs are spaced with a regular or thin space. Depending on the situation, some spacing of these symbols might be necessary in other languages — for example, when setting in all-caps.

According to GOST technical standards, Russian language uses the semicolon to denote time:

3.5.2 Elements presenting dates and time of the day are placed one after another without spacing.

Where needed, one may use the following symbols as separators:

- (dash) for separating the elements ‘year’ and ‘month’, ‘year’ and ‘week’, ‘year’ and ‘day’, ‘month’ and ‘day’, ‘week’ and ‘day’ as well as indicating omitted elements;

: (semicolon) for separating the elements of the time of the day (‘day’, ‘minute’, ‘minute and second’);

/ (slash) for separation in presenting the period of time;

# (number sign) for separating within the recurring period of time, periods of time, and recurring factor.
GOST ISO 8601–2001
Presenting dates and time. General requirements

However, using period for registering time or date should not be considered mistake in non-crucial situations.

Normally, the colon and the semicolon are not case-sensitive — the semicolon is fixed to the baseline due to its comma, and the colon usually follows this lead. Lifting just one of the pair looks quite weird:

The situations requiring a lifted colon are quite rare. The most common are denoting scale or time with lining figures. In such cases you can also adjust the colon manually.

Exclamation and question marks are most commonly designed of the cap-height. Like the other two-piece symbols, question and exclamation marks are spaced out in French. The exclamation mark is typically symmetrical and upright, while the question mark, depending on font and the face, may require additional kerning pairs.

The inverted exclamation mark and question mark are used in Spanish and some other languages, they can be lifted when setting in uppercase, if there is an applicable Opentype feature.

The 1960s saw an attempt to introduce the so-called interrobang — a combination of exclamation and question marks, intended for rhetorical questions. The interrobang is still drawn in many fonts, despite rarely being used as intended.

title: Atlassian tightens tracking of staff AI use as other technology firms encourage ‘tokenmaxxing’
description: Some companies reportedly using leaderboards for employees who used the most AI in their...
fullText:
Some companies reportedly using leaderboards for employees who used the most AI in their work

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Software firm Atlassian has sought to tighten tracking of its staff’s AI spending by introducing “wallets” with monthly caps of up $2,000 for each employee, amid an explosion in costs at other tech companies.

The move by Atlassian, which recently cited AI as part of the reason behind cutting 1,600 staff, bucks the trend of others in the tech sector who encouraged employees to use as much of the technology as possible, dubbed “tokenmaxxing”. Some companies have reportedly introduced leaderboards for employees who used the most AI in their work.

Tokens refer to the measurement of a response AI gives to a prompt. OpenAI has said one token is about four characters, and something like the US Declaration of Independence amounts to 1,695 tokens. OpenAI’s flagship model, GPT-5.6 Sol, has a charge of US$5 for every 1m tokens, while Anthropic’s Claude Fable and Mythos models are US$10 for every 1m tokens.

Under tokenmaxxing, the costs quickly add up.

Uber reportedly blew through its AI budget in four months, and Amazon has reportedly told employees to stop using AI just for the sake of using AI.

While Atlassian never encouraged tokenmaxxing or had unlimited AI budgets, the Australian company this month introduced an “AI wallet” for staff in the research and development team.

According to an internal memo seen by Guardian Australia, employees have between $500 and $2,000 monthly spend in the wallet, which can be used across four AI products, including Claude Code. Employees receive notifications as they approach their limit on their wallets, and usage is paused when the money runs out.

Employees can request additional funds. It is understood Atlassian has not turned down any request for additional funds so far.

A company spokesperson said it was transforming into an “AI-first company” by supporting people building and experimenting with the technology.

“Atlassian provides a significant budget for our builders to leverage multiple AI tools,” the spokesperson said.

“AI tooling budgets are set by role based on how different teams work.”

They said the wallet also represented a boost in the amount employees could spend.

A June PureProfile survey of 500 senior Australia staff at companies using AI, conducted on behalf of search AI company Elastic, found that 80% were concerned that high usage was being mistaken for productivity gains.

It found 32% had reported pausing, cancelling or winding back AI deployments, due to cost.

Elastic’s ANZ manager, Jeremy Pell, said a monthly cap on AI spend was “smart” and more organisations should be doing it.

“Right now, only 9% of Australian organisations currently have any limits on token or API consumption when it comes to AI agents or autonomous workflows, so any organisation that adopts this practice is an outlier,” he said.

Arun Chandrasekaran, a distinguished vice-president analyst at research firm Gartner, said wallets were a simple way to “incentivise the right behaviour” and stop people from using AI ineffectively.

He said such expenses were becoming an important issue among businesses, with the cost explosion being driven by AI agents that autonomously undertake tasks on behalf of the user.

“You suddenly have these systems that are all trying to do independent tasks that are spawning smaller agents, that are creating their own prompts and initiating requests for the model,” he said.

“So while the AI model prices have been falling for the last three years, the volume of tokens that particularly the AI agents are starting to send to the models … is significantly increasing.”

Chandrasekaran said companies are figuring out how to drive the cost down, including using less powerful models for simpler tasks, and looking at using open weight – where people can download and run the models on their own systems – or open source models.
